prompts.L5:
Please write a text about the following topic:

Keywords: There, Does, All

outputs.L1:
No one loves you more ... more ... more ...

There were sincere lies everywhere, placed directly before the next step. Does everyone pretend to be part of being alive?

I am proposing words — all structures have crumbled in earliest death. I’m crossing the yellow sands. It’s so hard to know without relating it to you: shaping a heart, taking hold of me, and someone says, “I don’t get it!”

You don’t have to have love — or you do. Which? I don’t think you do. Before the explosion, I was here without it, and I have been in many places loveless. I don’t want you to know what I’m really thinking — or do I? Before creation, when there might be no “I knew,” everything one has ever said is not quite true.

He or she betrays you. Why do you want to hurt me ... badly? Want to, or simply do? Treason was provoked everywhere, even here, by knowing one was one, and I was alone: a pale hue.

The sky of death is milky green today, like a poison pool near a desert mine. I picked prickly pear fruit and tasted it; then we drove on, maybe to Yarnell. These outposts where I grew up — I didn’t do that.

I have no ... identity, and love is an object to kick as you walk across the blazing bare ground, where ... sentimental, when what I love, I ... don’t have that one word.

This fire is all there is ... to find ... I find it. You have to find it. It isn’t love — it’s what?
outputs.L2:
Nobody cares for you more—more, more than this. Honest falsehoods were set everywhere, right in front of the following step. Is everyone acting, as part of being alive?

I am offering language: every framework has collapsed into the first kind of death. I am moving across the yellow sand. It is nearly impossible to understand unless I connect it to you: forming a heart, holding onto me, while someone says, “I don’t understand.”

You don’t need love—or maybe you do. Which is it? I don’t believe you do. Was this before the blast? I existed here without love, and I have lived in many places where love was absent.

I don’t want you to know what I truly think—or perhaps I do—before the beginning, when there may have been no such thing as “I knew.” Everything anyone has ever said is not entirely accurate.

He or she betrays you. Why do you want to wound me so badly? Do you want to, or does it simply happen? Betrayal was stirred up everywhere, even here, by the awareness that one was oneself, and that I was solitary, a washed-out color.

Today the sky of death is a cloudy green, like a toxic pool beside a desert mine. I picked fruit from a prickly pear and tasted it; afterward we kept driving, perhaps toward Yarnell. These were the remote places where I was raised. I did not do that.

I have no real identity, and love becomes a thing to kick along as you walk over the burning naked earth, where everything turns sentimental. Yet what I love—I do not have the exact word for it. This fire is all there is to discover. I discover it. You have to discover it too. It is not love. Then what is it?
outputs.L3:
The speaker reflects deeply on the question of whether love is truly necessary. Having lived in many places and passed through many experiences without it, they wonder if love is something essential or merely something people are taught to long for. This uncertainty gives the text a restless and searching quality. The speaker does not simply declare a need for love; instead, they examines the emptiness and survival that have shaped their life, asking whether what is missing can even be called love at all.

Throughout the text, truth and communication appear unstable. Words do not seem fully reliable, and nearly everything that is spoken feels partly false or incomplete. The speaker seems aware that language can distort feeling as much as it reveals it. This creates a sense of emotional distance, as though even honest speech cannot fully bridge the gap between one person and another. Communication becomes uncertain, fragile, and haunted by the possibility of misunderstanding.

The speaker also expresses a powerful fear of betrayal and pain. There is a sense that closeness may lead not to comfort but to injury. To love, or even to reach toward another person, means risking abandonment, disappointment, or harm. Beneath this fear lies the deeper loneliness of being a separate self: the painful awareness that no one can ever completely enter another person’s experience. The speaker longs for connection but is also frightened by the vulnerability that connection requires.

The imagery of deserts, poison-colored skies, and fire creates a bleak emotional landscape. These images suggest loss, danger, exhaustion, and spiritual desolation. The desert evokes barrenness and wandering, while the poisoned sky suggests a world made hostile or corrupted. Fire adds intensity, implying destruction as well as desire. Together, these images present the speaker’s inner life as a place of harsh searching, where hope exists only faintly and every movement forward carries the risk of pain.

Ultimately, the speaker struggles to name what they are truly seeking. Although love is the word that seems closest, it may not be precise enough. What the speaker wants may be safety, truth, recognition, belonging, or some form of peace that cannot easily be described. The text suggests that the deepest human needs are often difficult to name, and that the search for love may sometimes be a search for something even more mysterious: a way to feel whole, real, and less alone in the world.
outputs.L4:
The text presents a fragmented and deeply introspective exploration of alienation, fractured identity, betrayal, and uncertainty about love. Rather than developing its ideas in a linear or narrative way, it moves through a shifting, associative lyric voice that seems to wander between memory, landscape, and philosophical questioning. Images of the desert, emptiness, distance, and disorientation create a sense of emotional and spiritual isolation. The speaker appears to be searching for connection, but that search is constantly interrupted by doubt, pain, and an unstable sense of self.

A central concern of the text is the difficulty of knowing what love is, or even whether love can be clearly named. Love is not presented as a simple comfort or resolution. Instead, it appears uncertain, wounded, and perhaps already connected to betrayal or loss. The speaker seems to desire intimacy, but this desire is complicated by mistrust and by the fear that love may be an illusion, a memory, or a word that fails to contain the depth of human need. Because of this, love remains unstable throughout the text: it is longed for, questioned, resisted, and never fully secured.

The fragmented form of the lyric voice reflects the speaker’s fractured identity. The movement from one image or thought to another suggests a consciousness struggling to hold itself together. Memories surface in pieces, and the self appears divided between past and present, desire and disillusionment, hope and emptiness. This fragmentation gives the text its emotional intensity. The speaker is not simply describing alienation from others, but also alienation from the self. There is a sense that identity has been damaged or made uncertain by experience, especially by betrayal and by the failure of familiar meanings to provide stability.

Desert imagery plays an important role in shaping this atmosphere. The desert suggests barrenness, exposure, and solitude, but it can also suggest a place of revelation. In such a landscape, there is nowhere to hide. The speaker is forced to confront emptiness directly, both in the world and within the self. The desert becomes more than a physical setting; it becomes a symbolic space where the speaker encounters the limits of language, memory, and emotional certainty. Its vastness mirrors the speaker’s inner uncertainty and the difficulty of finding a clear path toward meaning.

The text’s existential questioning deepens its treatment of love. The speaker’s search is not only for romantic affection or personal reassurance, but for something more fundamental: a reason to continue, a way to understand the self, and a way to live with emptiness. Love matters because it represents the possibility of connection, but the text refuses to reduce meaning to love alone. Instead, it suggests that the speaker must confront a deeper crisis beneath the desire for affection. The real question is not simply whether love exists, but whether love can survive betrayal, whether identity can survive fragmentation, and whether meaning can be found in a world that feels uncertain and estranged.

Ultimately, the text portrays love as unresolved and perhaps unnamed. Its significance lies in this very instability. Love is not offered as an easy answer, but as part of a larger struggle with emptiness, selfhood, and meaning. Through its fragmented lyric structure and stark imagery, the text reveals a speaker searching for connection while also recognizing the insufficiency of conventional ideas of affection. What emerges is a powerful meditation on the human need to be known, to belong, and to find meaning even when language, memory, and love itself seem unreliable.
outputs.L5: There is a quiet strength in taking small steps every day. Does progress always happen quickly? Not at all. Sometimes growth is slow, and sometimes it is hard to see, but every effort matters. All meaningful change begins with a decision to keep going, even when the path is uncertain. There will be challenges, but patience and determination can make a difference. In the end, all we can do is try our best and learn from each experience.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write an experimental free-verse poem in a fragmented, stream-of-consciousness style about love, identity, betrayal, death, and a desert road trip through Arizona.
counterfactuals.output:
we took the borrowed car west  
or south  
or into the mouth of something

Arizona opened like a cut map

red rock / gas station / heat shimmer /  
your hand on the wheel  
my name in your mouth  
not my name exactly  
the one you used when you wanted me soft

love is a motel mirror with fingerprints  
love is ice melting in a paper cup  
love is you saying  
look  
and me looking  
even when the sky had nothing left to prove

*

I remember the road

not as road but as sentence  
unpunctuated  
running on and on past saguaros  
past the bleached ribs of something unlucky  
past billboards for jerky / Jesus / fireworks /  
past the place where you said  
I don’t know who you are anymore

and I thought

good

good

maybe I am escaping myself at last

*

identity:  
a wallet full of expired cards  
a photograph where my face is always arriving late  
the name my mother gave me  
the name you took apart  
the name I buried under a cairn outside Sedona

I was someone’s daughter  
someone’s lover  
someone’s alibi  
someone’s ghost rehearsing the body

you were driving too fast

the desert did not care

*

at a diner near Flagstaff  
you lied with your whole mouth

eggs congealed  
coffee burned  
a fly performed its small apocalypse against the window

I watched you say her name  
by not saying it

the waitress refilled the silence

outside, the car ticked in the heat  
like a bomb reconsidering itself

*

betrayal is not a knife

too clean

betrayal is sand in the teeth  
is the receipt found folded into your jeans  
is the second toothbrush  
is the way the landscape keeps going  
even after the world ends

I wanted thunder

instead:  
a lizard on a rock  
a plastic bag in a mesquite tree  
your sunglasses reflecting two versions of me  
both stupid  
both holy  
both leaving

*

somewhere near Winslow  
we stopped for gas

you went inside  
I stood under the awning  
watching black birds stitch the sky shut

death had been traveling with us for miles

not dramatic  
not robed  
no scythe

just the smell of hot rubber  
a white cross leaning by the shoulder  
the radio naming a crash on I-40  
the small dead moths gathered in the grille  
like prayers that misread the light

I thought of my father  
how his hands looked after  
how the body becomes object  
how love keeps talking to it anyway

*

I wanted to forgive you

no

I wanted to become the kind of person  
who could forgive you  
and be admired by myself  
in the ruins

no

I wanted you to suffer

no

I wanted the desert to enter us  
with its terrible honesty  
its bone-colored grammar  
its refusal to bloom on command

*

night came violet

then absolute

the highway unspooled beneath the headlights  
a film of a film of a memory  
you humming along to a song you claimed to hate

I pressed my forehead to the glass

inside the window  
my reflection floated over the desert  
transparent  
unfaithful  
alive

who am I if not the wound I keep decorating

who am I if not the hand reaching back  
toward the person  
who pushed me

*

in Tucson the air smelled like dust and oranges

we slept back-to-back  
in a room with a broken lamp  
and a painting of a canyon  
more convincing than our peace

you dreamed loudly

I lay awake counting your breaths

not because I loved you  
though I did  
not because I feared you would die  
though you will  
though I will  
though everyone we passed on the highway  
was practicing disappearance

I counted because numbers make a fence  
because a body beside you  
is still a body  
even after trust has left it

*

morning

sun like a verdict

I bought water  
you bought cigarettes  
we said almost nothing  
which was our most fluent language

the road waited

long  
white  
merciless

I got in

not because I chose you

because the self is sometimes a passenger  
because leaving is a country  
you must enter mile by mile  
because love, even ruined, has inertia  
because the desert had not finished with my name

*

outside Phoenix  
the heat rose in visible waves

the city appeared  
glass / asphalt / palm trees imported from someone else’s dream

you asked  
where now

and I laughed

not kindly

not cruelly

like a door opening in an empty house

nowhere, I said

everywhere

pull over

*

the shoulder of the road  
gravel popping under the tires  
semis roaring past like gods with deadlines

I stepped out

the sun touched every part of me  
without tenderness  
without shame

you said my name

that old name

small in your mouth now  
a coin worn thin

I let it fall

the desert took it

I walked until your voice became heat  
until heat became light  
until light became a white animal  
running ahead of me

and I followed

not saved  
not dead  
not yours

still breaking

still becoming

still moving through Arizona  
with my shadow unfastened behind me.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a surreal prose-poem that sounds like someone thinking aloud after heartbreak, with broken syntax, repeated words, ellipses, and images of yellow sands, prickly pear, Yarnell, poison-colored sky, and fire.
counterfactuals.output:
I keep finding yellow sands in my mouth, like I’ve been speaking desert all night, like every word got down on its knees and crawled away from me...

you said love and I heard fire.

no, no—  
I heard the small crackle before fire, the dry yes of grass, the match-head heart, the thing in me that wanted to be lit because being warm seemed close enough to being held.

Yarnell sits somewhere in my ribs. A little town of ash. A road bending. A silence with black boots on. I pass it every time I think of you, which is often, which is not at all, which is often.

The sky was poison-colored that day—green-yellow, bruise-gold, the exact shade of don’t go, don’t go, don’t go—  
and the prickly pear held up its flat palms like witnesses. Even the cactus knew. Even the spines leaned closer.

I am talking to no one.  
I am talking to the stove flame.  
I am talking to the sand because sand remembers how to fall apart and still be everywhere.

After you, my hands became two little burned houses. My name became smoke trying to spell itself. I walked and walked and the yellow sands followed, shuffling behind me, whispering: lost, lost, lost...

But maybe lost is a place.  
Maybe Yarnell is a place.  
Maybe the body is a place where fire learns your address and keeps coming back with flowers made of sparks.

I told myself: do not touch.  
I touched.

I told myself: do not look for water in the prickly pear, do not bite sweetness from a thing made to wound you.  
I bit. I bled. I said thank you because heartbreak makes a church out of anything sharp enough.

The poison-colored sky opened its mouth. No rain. Only more sky. Only that awful yellow. Only the fire rehearsing your voice in the mesquite, saying come here, saying stay, saying nothing, nothing, nothing...

And I keep thinking—  
if love was real, why did it leave teeth in everything?

The sands shift. The cactus blooms like a secret it should have kept. Somewhere, in Yarnell, wind moves through the blackened grass, and I am still there, stupid with smoke, holding the match, holding the absence, holding the little flame of your name until it eats me clean.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Compose an avant-garde poem in the style of contemporary confessional/Language poetry, exploring whether love is necessary, with disjointed lines and unsettling desert imagery.
counterfactuals.output:
**IS LOVE NECESSARY IN THE ERG**

I put my mouth to the sand  
and it answered with my mother’s teeth.

No,  
said the cactus,  
but it kept its water hidden.

The sky was a blue surgical sheet.  
Under it:  
my little organs of wanting,  
laid out in alphabetical disorder.

Love is necessary  
the way a mirage is necessary  
to the dying animal—

not for arrival,  
but for the cruel grammar of forward.

I have been tender  
as a scorpion in a teacup.  
I have been held  
and mistaken that for rescue.

Listen:  
the dunes keep rearranging  
their evidence.

A shoe appears.  
A ribcage.  
A word like *beloved*  
bleached until it means  
bone / burden / borrow.

In the distance,  
a motel sign flickers  
VACANCY  
VACANCY  
VAC—

and inside me  
the old room refuses to empty.

If love is not necessary,  
why does the vulture circle  
with such ceremonial patience?

If love is necessary,  
why does it leave  
salt in the bed  
and call it weather?

I confess:  
I wanted a hand  
not because I was falling  
but because falling  
had become my only language.

The desert opens its dry book.  
Every page says thirst.  
Every page says endure.  
Every page says  
you can live without this.

Then night comes,  
black animal,  
licking the heat from the stones,

and somewhere beneath the sand  
a root goes on  
drinking  
from an invisible wound.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Create a fractured monologue from a speaker who feels loveless and unsure of their identity, mixing philosophical questions about “I,” betrayal, creation, and death with Southwestern landscape details.
counterfactuals.output:
I keep saying **I** like it is a stake driven into the ground.

I.

Here, in this red country, stakes don’t hold. The soil loosens. The wind worries everything free. Fence wire sings all night over the arroyos, and the mesquite leans like a witness that has forgotten the crime.

Who is it that says **I**?

A mouth. A thirst. A body carrying its own shadow across caliche and dust. A thing assembled from other people’s refusals.

I was loved, I think. Or I was near love. Or I mistook heat for it, the way a desert traveler mistakes a sheet of light for water. There was someone’s hand once at the back of my neck. Someone’s voice saying stay, saying only you, saying trust me with the careful cruelty of a man sharpening a knife in another room.

Betrayal is not a door slamming.

No.

It is the house remaining exactly where it was while every room changes its name.

The kitchen becomes a courtroom. The bed becomes a grave. The mirror becomes an animal you do not recognize, staring back with your own eyes and asking: what did you think you were?

I thought I was beloved.

There. That is the foolishness. That is the little clay idol I made and breathed into. My own creation, my own false god. I gathered scraps—one promise, one night of rain, one laugh under a neon sign outside a gas station in Lordsburg—and I shaped them into a life. I said: let there be us. And for a while there was.

For a while.

Even God must have known the shame of making something that could leave.

The sky out here is too large for comfort. It exposes the soul. At dusk the mountains bruise purple, and the ocotillo lift their thorned arms like they are surrendering to nobody. Coyotes start up beyond the wash, laughing their thin, metallic laughter. I envy them. They know what they are. Hunger with teeth. Voices braided to the dark.

But me?

I am divided. I am the betrayed and the betrayer. The maker and the ruin. The question and the mouth that cannot stop asking.

If I say I am loveless, who is the one deprived?

If I say I am dead, who is still speaking?

Death has been walking beside me for years, not in a black robe, no, nothing so theatrical. Death wears sun-bleached denim. Death has cracked lips. Death buys coffee at dawn from a truck stop outside Tucson and stands with me watching ravens pick at something unnameable on the shoulder of the road.

Death says: you are not special.

And I say: thank God.

And then I weep, because I wanted to be. To someone. To one living soul. I wanted my name to alter the weather in another chest. I wanted to be the reason a hand paused over a phone, the reason a car turned back, the reason a prayer—if prayers are real—caught fire before it left the tongue.

But no one turned back.

The desert does not turn back either. It just goes on becoming itself. Sand into glass under lightning. Bones into mineral. Flowers out of nothing after rain, obscene and brief, yellow cups opening in the gravel as if resurrection were easy.

Is creation always this violent?

A child from blood. A poem from loneliness. A self from abandonment. The world from whatever silence existed before the world.

Maybe there was never an **I**. Maybe there was only weather passing through a shape. A temporary arrangement of ache and appetite. My mother’s fear, my father’s absence, my lover’s lie, my own hands trying to build a shelter from the very wood of the cross.

Listen.

The wind is dragging tumbleweed against the cattle guard. The moon is caught in the ribs of a saguaro. Somewhere far off, a train moves through the dark with its one long note of mourning, as if distance itself had been wounded.

I want to forgive.

No, that is not true.

I want forgiveness to descend on me without my participation. I want it to arrive like monsoon rain over the Chihuahuan desert, sudden and muscular, hammering the dust flat, filling the dry creek beds, making every creosote bush release that sharp green smell like the earth remembering it has a body.

But forgiveness is work, they say.

So is identity.

So is staying alive.

Every morning I wake and reconstruct the person who was destroyed the night before. I fit the ribs around the breath. I hang the face back on its hook. I speak my name until it sounds almost human.

I.

I.

I.

A match struck in a canyon.

A footprint filling with sand.

A god made of mud asking its maker why it was made breakable.

And if love does not come again? If no voice calls me home from the edge of myself? If I die here, unnamed even by my own heart, beneath a sky extravagant with stars that do not care?

Then let the vultures have their scripture.

Let the juniper hold my last confession.

Let the desert take me apart gently, grain by grain, until there is no wound and no witness, no lover and no lie, no question left of who I was.

Only red earth.

Only wind.

Only the vast, indifferent mercy of being nothing

and still having been.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a chaotic lyrical passage that begins “No one loves you more ... more ... more ...” and develops into an abstract meditation on love as something unreachable, using repetition and incomplete sentences.
counterfactuals.output:
No one loves you more ... more ... more ...

than the room after you leave it,  
than the echo chewing its own mouth,  
than the light that arrives too late to touch your face.

Love, love, love—  
a ladder painted on the wall.  
A door with no house behind it.  
A hand reaching through water and finding only the idea of a hand.

More ... more ...  
as if more could become nearer,  
as if saying it again could build a bridge,  
as if the bridge did not keep dissolving, plank by plank, breath by breath—

I loved you from the far side of impossible.  
From the window that never opened.  
From the beginning after the ending.  
From the place where all names go soft and useless.

And still.  
And still.  
And still the heart runs forward, barefoot, blind, calling—

you, you, you—

but love is not there.  
Not there exactly.  
Not absent either.  
A star behind the fog.  
A song under the floorboards.  
A mouth saying come closer from the other side of forever.

No one loves you more ... more ... more ...

but more is a horizon,  
and the horizon is always leaving,  
and leaving is the shape love takes  
when it wants to be worshiped,  
when it wants to remain pure,  
when it wants to remain unreachable—

almost touched,  
almost known,  
almost mine,

never.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
